title: Help & Support
subtitle: Product help, usage guidance and support contact.

gettingStarted.title: Getting Started
gettingStarted.body: Sign in with the email and password your administrator set up for you. The first time (and whenever they change), you're shown what PROSM Time records about you and asked to acknowledge the Privacy Policy and Terms of Use. On the Dashboard, use Clock In to start your shift and Clock Out to end it - a live map shows your current position and, when relevant, the site's work area. The app opens in your device's language when it's one of the nine supported; you can change it any time from the user menu. Employees open to their own home page: clock in and out, their hours today, this week (from Sunday) and this month, and the bar at the bottom with attendance and leave (in My file) and allowances. The Owner, Managers and Supervisors open to the Dashboard. The Owner doesn't clock in or out.

attendance.title: Clocking In & Out
attendance.body:
Choose your site (and project, if applicable) before clocking in - or leave Site empty and describe where you actually are if you're not at a registered location. Some sites require a photo, held steady for a moment so the app can confirm it's a live capture, not an old or static image. Right before anything is submitted, a confirmation screen shows exactly what's about to be recorded - your photo (if one was taken), your GPS location, the site/workplace and the time - with two optional fields, a note and your activity, which your manager can see. The time recorded is always the server's time, not your phone's clock. Clocking in is blocked on a day your approved leave covers. On the phone app, PROSM Time also reminds you itself - even when the app is closed: shortly after your shift's end if you're still clocked in, and a few minutes before your next scheduled shift. If your organisation turned it on, opening the app inside a registered site asks “You are at …. Clock in now?”; nothing is recorded without your answer, and if you agree you go through the usual steps (and the photo, if required). If your site has end-of-shift tasks, their list appears before you clock out.

New: the clock-in screen is a full map with a see-through card for your status and shift timer; the clock-in, clock-out, break and change-site buttons are see-through above the bottom bar, with a floating 🆘 button. You choose the site (or type your place) in the confirm screen itself. Clocking in needs a live location from the phone, and is refused outside a site that blocks outside clock-ins (new sites start with a 250 m zone).

walkInGeofence.title: Working at a Site You're Not Assigned To
walkInGeofence.body: The site list starts with the best match for you: the site you are assigned to; if you are not assigned and stand inside a registered site, that site, marked “you are here today”; otherwise “No site”. The other sites follow, nearest first. Clocking in without a site stays available, and your clock-in point then becomes the centre of the organisation’s work area for the rest of the shift.

siteChange.title: Changing Sites Mid-Shift
siteChange.body: Change Site is its own button on the Dashboard whenever you're clocked in - no need to pause first. Pick where you've moved to (or leave Site empty), and the move is recorded with the time it happened. You're never clocked out in the process. The record keeps both sites: the first site, then each change with its time, also in the notes and the PDF. From the change on, "inside / outside the work area" is checked against the new site.

sos.title: SOS / Emergency
sos.body: The SOS button is on the Dashboard during every shift once your clock-in is confirmed. Pressing it sends a high-priority alert with your location to your site's managers, the Owner and co-workers clocked in at the same site, and it's logged in the Emergency Log. SOS is not an emergency service - it doesn't call the police or an ambulance. In an emergency, always call your local emergency number. It needs an internet connection. If you work without a chosen site, the managers of the nearest site receive it. When an SOS reaches you, "Show location" opens where it was sent from on the map, and "Silence" stops the siren and keeps the alert on screen until you close it. "View the emergency log" shows only for the owner and managers. On the Android app an SOS rings with the alarm tone even when the phone is on silent and opens on the whole screen over the lock screen, until you open or silence it (two minutes at most).

notifications.title: How Notifications Reach the Right Person
notifications.body: If you clock in or out - or move during your shift - outside your work area, you're asked to explain why, and the right person is notified: an employee's situation reaches that site's manager (and the Owner); a manager's own situation goes straight to the Owner. Tap a notification to jump to what it's about.

timesheets.title: Timesheets
timesheets.body: Once your manager generates a timesheet for a period, it appears under Timesheets for you to review and submit for approval. Worked time, breaks and overtime are shown as separate totals - break time is never subtracted from your worked hours, and overtime starts at the time your site's policy defines. Once approved, a timesheet is locked; if it needs a correction, request one from the timesheet's page.

exceptions.title: Reviews - Exceptions, Corrections, Offline Times and Fake Locations
exceptions.body:
Everything that needs a manager's decision appears in the Manager Console under Pending Review: out-of-zone exceptions (with your reason), correction requests, actions recorded offline with the device's time, and locations reported as fake. If an exception is approved you're treated as present the full time. If it's rejected, your effective worked time is capped at the moment the situation was first detected. Flags are information for a person to review fairly - not automatic decisions.

New: My file → Attendance → Exceptions lists your exceptions and where each stands (pending review, approved, rejected), and lets you send your reason.

allowances.title: Allowances
allowances.body:
Press "Fill from my attendance": every day you attended is filled from your allowance prices (that day's site, then your category, then your own prices). Overtime is paid from the exact minutes (15 minutes at 100 an hour = 25), and hours still waiting for a manager's review are not counted. Add only what has no price, such as travel, check the totals and submit; your manager approves or returns it with a note. While reviewing, a manager with the right permission can change a line on the sheet - each change needs a reason, the totals update at once, and the change (before, after, who, why) is kept; nothing can be changed once the sheet is approved, unless an approved sheet is reopened with a reason. The PDF marks every changed value with *, lists the changes, highlights public holidays and shows any unpaid-leave deductions (taken from pay, not from allowances). Prices are set under Allowances > Prices: per site, per employee category and per person, plus the overtime hour and the extra day. A day without attendance (travel, an errand) can be given its site - in its cell or its detail - and is priced at that site. "Apply the current prices" prices your open days again after the prices change. The sheet also downloads as an Excel file.

New: the period summary on top - the total, the number of days, where they stand (draft, sent, approved) and a coloured bar showing what the money is made of. The period and the export buttons sit in one bar. An employee takes their sheet as PDF only; Excel and print are for those who approve allowances.

kiosk.title: Kiosk Mode
kiosk.body: Open Kiosk Mode from the sidebar and pick a site to turn a shared tablet or computer into its clock-in screen for external workers (people without an app account - everyone with an account clocks in from the app). The worker types the 6-digit number the app made for them on the Workers page, then taps Clock in or Clock out; the screen returns to the keypad after each action. While the kiosk is open the device is locked to it: there's no menu, other pages and the back button lead back to the kiosk, and leaving needs the password of the account that opened it (the Exit kiosk button). Kiosk Mode is opened by the Owner, or by a Manager for a site they manage.

reportsCenter.title: Reports Center
reportsCenter.body:
Pick a report type, a date range and, where relevant, an employee or site, then export it as a PDF. Reports include Attendance Record (offline device times are marked), Allowances, Workforce, Contractor, Site, Late Arrivals, Missed Checkouts, Leave Conflicts, Manager Overrides and Location Violations - which now lists being outside the work area (with the employee's reason and review status), implausible locations and fake locations together. A Manager sees only the sites they manage; the Owner sees the whole organisation. Next to every PDF download there is a Print button. In the PDF, a page never cuts through a row, the column headings repeat on each page and the pages are numbered. The same page has "External labour cost" - each external worker with their contractor, pay, how they are paid (hour/day/week/month/year), days and hours from the kiosk and the total for the period - and "External labour attendance". Employees' pay and its reports are on the Payroll page.

New: the Reports page is for those who manage; an employee exports their attendance, timesheets and allowances from those pages. "Labour cost" in Reports covers external labour only, with totals per currency.

sites.title: Sites (Administrators)
sites.body: Sites is where work sites are set up and people are assigned. Adding a site needs only a name, its location - stand there and press Use my current location - the radius and whether a photo is required; everything else is under More options. A new site takes your device's time zone. When you assign someone, their role at the site starts from their organisation role - a Manager or Supervisor becomes the site's manager, so they see its people. Everything else about a site is on its own page, under Site rules: GPS tolerance, shift hours, overtime and late-deduction times, break rounding, ongoing presence monitoring, exempt employees, and the self-service blocks (once lateness starts counting, clock-out outside the work area, clock-in outside the work area). In the site form, say whose site it is - the company's own or a client's (type the client's name; names already used are suggested) - and what kind it is: office, warehouse, construction site, factory, shop / branch, or another kind you name. If someone sent you the site's location, paste the link (a Google Maps link, short ones too) or the coordinates under "Or paste a location link" and press "Use the link" - that becomes the site's location.

workers.title: External Workers
workers.body: Workers (in the sidebar, for the Owner and anyone who manages sites) is where you add people who work for you without an app account - contractors or day labour. Type the name (and the contractor, if any) and press Add: the app creates the worker's 6-digit number and shows it so you can copy it and give it to them. Workers belong to the whole organisation, not to one site: they clock in and out with their number at the kiosk of any site, and the list shows where each one is clocked in right now. You can force a clock-out (with a reason) if someone forgot, and deactivate a worker - a deactivated number stops working at the kiosk.

settingsCenter.title: Settings (Owner)
settingsCenter.body: The sidebar is grouped as Field operations (attendance, sites, leave and holidays, shifts, kiosk), Human resources, Payroll, Reports and analytics, and Administration and governance; every page keeps its old address, so saved links and notifications still open. Settings come in the same order: Organisation (the plan and activation code, the work calendar), Sites and clocking (each site's rules, the work area for clocking without a site, refusing fake locations, saying when someone opens the app inside a site, and the values every new site starts with), Attendance and leave (working time, overtime, leave types), Payroll (payroll settings and the external labour pay policy) and Security and governance (the action log, data retention). Each section shows only what you may change.

leave.title: Leave and permissions
leave.body: Request leave from the Leave tab of My file (or the Leave button at the bottom): your balance, the request, short permissions and your requests are there. Choose the type, the dates and, if you like, a reason (please leave out unnecessary health details). Types and their days are set by the Owner under Settings > Leave types. Your balance per type shows used and remaining days. When you request leave, choose who receives it - your site's manager or the Owner - from the list; only that person is notified and emailed, and you get a copy. Their answer - approved (with the dates and your remaining balance), declined, or cancelled after approval - comes back to you by notification and email, on the same email conversation. A manager can also turn an absence into leave from the dashboard's "Absent today" sheet ("Make it leave"), for example when you asked by phone: it is approved at once, past days too, and your timesheet follows. Approved leave can be cancelled only before its first day - from that day on, no one can cancel it, not even the Owner. Unpaid leave: the manager sets the deduction per day when approving; it is recorded automatically and shows in the payroll export and your allowance sheet, and it is reversed if the leave is cancelled before it starts. Only working days count: weekly rest days and public holidays inside the dates are not deducted from the balance, and a request made only of such days is refused with the reason. Before you send, you see the days that will be deducted and those counted as holidays. The Leave page in the menu is the owner's alone: every leave of the organisation in one place. The owner takes no leave. Requests are approved in the manager console.

schedule.title: Shift Roster
schedule.body:
See your upcoming shifts on the Schedule page. Authorised managers create ready-made shifts per site and assign people, including overnight shifts (marked “(+1)”); overlapping shifts are refused. The same page has open shifts (a manager posts a shift with no one on it, people at the site ask for it, the manager picks one), swapping a shift with a colleague with the manager’s approval, the schedule’s estimated cost, and each site’s end-of-shift tasks.

New: for managers the schedule is a whole week - a row per person, a column per day, each shift a block in its template's colour with its hours, and ✓ when it was worked or "Not worked". Move between weeks with the arrows. Press + in an empty cell to add a shift for that person and day, and pick several days to add them at once; press a shift to cancel it.

calendar.title: Hijri or Gregorian Calendar
calendar.body: Every date can show as Gregorian or Hijri - choose from the user menu, next to Language and Appearance. It's a per-device preference.

permissions.title: Permissions and Clocking On Behalf (Administrators)
permissions.body: Each person's page under People shows their permissions; whoever may change them can grant, revoke or reset one, with a reason. The Owner has every permission and can give any of them to anyone below. A Manager can give a Supervisor at their own sites a permission the Manager holds, and take it back. Approving leave and clocking someone in or out on their behalf are for the Owner and Managers only - never for oneself, and only for people below you at the sites you manage. Every change is recorded with who made it. The owner can also give a person all of the owner's authority with the "Organisation owner's authority" button on their page: every permission, the owner-only actions and every notification and email the owner receives, without changing the owner's own. It needs a reason, the person is told, and it is in the action log; once the owner withdraws it, the person is back to their role and their own permissions. The owner can also delegate for a set period - from a start to an end date - (for only some permissions, use the single switches), and the history shows under the button; it ends by itself and can be withdrawn early. Actions that could end the organisation (managing permissions, closing or deleting it, the licence and API keys) stay with the owner. Nobody decides their own request. A person's role can also be changed there, with a reason: the permissions follow at once, below manager they stop managing sites, and the direct grants still in place are listed for review.

getTheApp.title: Getting PROSM Time
getTheApp.body: On an Android phone: install PROSM Time from Google Play; it updates from there. If you have the older version that was downloaded from prosm.net, uninstall it first, then install from Google Play - your data is kept on the server. On any computer, tablet or iPhone: open https://time.prosm.net in the browser (you can add it to the home screen); it updates itself. They are all the same PROSM Time with the same account.

liveMap.title: Live Map
liveMap.body: The Dashboard shows a map with your current position and, once you're clocked in or have a site selected, a circle marking that site's work area, so you can see where you stand before clocking in or out.

radio.title: Why There's a Radio in PROSM Time
radio.body: Play a station on your way to work, and PROSM Time is already open when you arrive - a small nudge against the most common attendance mistake: forgetting to clock in. It sends no personal data. Its first list comes from the stations of the country your phone's time zone points to (Egypt, the Gulf, Europe, America...), kept for a day so it opens at once.

offline.title: Working Without Internet
offline.body: On your phone, Clock In, Clock Out, breaks and Change Site work with no connection; a small card tells you you're offline, and a bar shows how many actions are waiting. They're kept encrypted on the device and sent automatically, once, when the connection returns. Because these were recorded without the server, they keep your device's time: if it differs from the server's by more than 2 minutes, the action is marked "Device time (offline)" and your manager reviews it. A time earlier than your last recorded action, or on a day of approved leave, is refused - ask your manager to correct it. Other pages need a connection; if one can't load, the app tells you and lets you try again.

locationChecks.title: Work Areas and Fake Locations
locationChecks.body: Each site has a work area (a circle on the map). Clocking in or out outside it is recorded as an exception and you're asked why; one reason covers the whole trip, even if both your clock-out and your next clock-in were outside. A site can also be set to refuse a self clock-in from outside its area - then ask your manager to clock you in. On Android, PROSM Time notices when the location comes from a mock-location (fake GPS) app: it's recorded and reviewed by your manager, and your organisation may choose to refuse it. Faking your location or your phone's time is against the Terms of Use.

privacy.title: Your Privacy
privacy.body: PROSM Time records your location when you clock in or out, take a break, change site or send an SOS. It is also recorded about every 5 minutes during your shift only - on Android also in the background, even with the app closed, after telling you first and with a visible notification - and it always stops when you clock out. A photo is taken only where your site requires one; there's no facial recognition. Your organisation's managers see your records. Location samples are deleted after 30 days and photos after 90 days. You can withdraw location or camera permission in your device settings at any time. For your rights over your data, ask your organisation first, or write to info@prosm.net. Full details are in the Privacy Policy and Terms of Use below. The owner can shorten retention in Settings > Data and privacy. When your account signs in from a new device, you are alerted, and so is the owner.

workCalendar.title: Work Calendar: Holidays, Rest Days and Special Days
workCalendar.body: From the Calendar page, those allowed set the public holidays (for the whole organisation or one site), the weekly rest days (organisation, site or shift) and special days (for example Ramadan hours or an early finish). Work on a public holiday or a rest day counts as overtime at the rate set for that kind of day, and nobody is marked absent or late on it. On a special day the start and end follow that day, so leaving early as agreed causes no deduction. Days are counted in the site's own time zone. Holidays also show on the dashboard and in reports and exports.

longSessions.title: Long Sessions and Hours Awaiting Review
longSessions.body: If you are still clocked in after 12 hours (the Owner can change this), the app asks once whether you are still working; you can answer "still working" or clock out. After 24 hours the session is closed automatically - its hours are kept but marked as awaiting review: they are not counted in totals, pay, allowances or cost until a manager reviews them, sets the real clock-out time with a reason, or extends the session. They show in "Needs review" for managers and in the reports as "closed automatically, awaiting review".

overtimeControl.title: Overtime, Lateness and Permissions
overtimeControl.body: You can ask for permission to arrive late or leave early from your day's page; an approved permission (paid) means no deduction for that time. A manager can also mark time as "not counted as overtime". Depending on the Owner's setting, overtime counts at once or only after a manager approves it - until then it shows as waiting and is left out of totals and allowances. The overtime rates for a workday, a rest day, a public holiday and night work are settings. Every manual adjustment to a day needs a reason, is recorded, and nothing changes on a period that is already approved.

liveCheck.title: Attendance Photo and Live Check
liveCheck.body: Where a site asks for a photo, it is taken from the live camera only - not chosen from the gallery. Where the phone supports it, a short live check asks you to turn your head or move closer; nothing of your face is stored except the photo itself and the result, and no video is sent. If the check fails or the phone cannot do it, your clock-in is still recorded and simply marked for your manager to look at (as is a stale or reused photo, or a location that looks too exact). The manager accepts, rejects with a reason, or asks you about it. The Owner or a manager can exempt a person from the live check.

leavingSite.title: Leaving the Site While Clocked In
leavingSite.body: Each site decides what happens when you leave its work area while clocked in: you get a notification asking whether to clock out (you can answer "still working", for example for an errand). On sites set to clock out at the time you left, a reminder follows if you do not answer, and when you agree your clock-out is recorded at the moment you left - nobody is ever clocked out without agreeing. Field workers can be exempted. Every such clock-out is recorded and can be corrected by a manager. On Android a small notification "PROSM Time · clocked in" stays visible while location is recorded - only during your shift, on its own silent channel.

managerDashboard.title: The Dashboard (Owner and managers)
managerDashboard.body:
The Owner and whoever holds "View the dashboard" see: an SOS bar (until someone acknowledges it), chips for what is waiting (only when there is something), the figures with a comparison to the previous period only when there is data for it, the sites map with each site's work area and who is there now, the sites table with external workers under each site, the approvals queue, people by role, scheduled vs actual, allowances and estimated cost (only with "View estimated cost") and the action log. Choose the organisation, your sites or yourself, and the period; the map and "here now" are live and not filtered by period. It refreshes every minute, and tapping the logo while on the dashboard refreshes it at once without losing your choices. Hover over a figure to see what it counts. "Absent today" and "On leave today" are separate cards: absent means expected with no attendance and no approved leave. "Not clocked out" lists who is still clocked in an hour after their shift (or the site's day) ended, and sessions left open from an earlier day. "Customise widgets" hides or reorders cards, saved to your account. Each figure opens the people behind it, with a button to the full page. The map's zoom buttons sit on the other side from the full-screen and all-sites buttons. The Insights card shows punctuality, lateness and absence. The owner gets a morning summary at 7 site time, an alert when someone misses a shift, and an alert when someone is still clocked in after their shift (15 minutes by default, set in Settings).

New: every figure card has one shape - icon, the figure with its unit, one line of context and the arrow against the previous period (the full sentence on hover); a card turns amber or red when someone is late, absent or not clocked out. "Planned vs actual" is now "Working hours trend": actual and scheduled totals and the adherence above the chart, today marked. "Attendance indicators" are three cards with charts: the rate as a ring, and repeat late and repeat overtime as bars per person. The "Shift ratings" card turns the faces people choose after clocking out into a KPI: the satisfaction score (great 100, normal 50, tough 0), by site, by client and by day - for the period chosen at the top (day, week, month or custom). The "Documents" card is full width: the counts, who has a document expiring or expired and how many days are left, and "No documents" while no document types are set up.

peopleAndPhotos.title: People, Roles and Profile Photos
peopleAndPhotos.body: The People page groups everyone by role - managers (with the Owner), supervisors, employees, viewers, then any custom role - each group with its count, which you can fold. One search and the site, status and shift filters work across all groups. Each person shows their profile photo (or their initial), role, site, shift and whether they are here now. A manager sees only the people at the sites they manage. Your profile photo is set from your profile; it is not the attendance photo, and it is shown only to people in your organisation.

phoneNotifications.title: Notifications and Reminders on the Phone
phoneNotifications.body: All PROSM Time notifications carry the same small PROSM icon. Your own clock-in/out reminders are set from the dashboard card. Android 14 and later may not allow exact alarms; a reminder can then arrive a few minutes late - the card says so and has a button to allow exact alarms. If location tracking cannot start (permission refused or location turned off), the app tells you and offers to try again or open the settings; your clock-in itself is never lost. The update notice can be swiped away.

subscription.title: Plan and subscription (owner)
subscription.body:
There are four plans: Starter (clocking, live map, SOS and radio; up to 3 sites; owner, one manager and employees), Business (+ announcements, departments, leave and permissions, scheduling, timesheets, allowances, kiosk, external labour and reports), Pro (+ payroll, labour cost, audit log and detailed permissions) and Enterprise (+ API, delegation and data retention control). The 30-day free trial is Enterprise in full. Billing is per employee per month, and every 10 external workers count as one user; the number of external workers allowed comes with your licence and shows on the plan card with "Billed users".

Settings > Subscription shows your plan and what it includes, employees against the limit, sites, the end date and how far back records are shown. Any change or renewal of the licence is made by PROSM: you get a notification and an email with the new licence as a PDF, and it applies at once. The activation code box appears only on a trial or after the licence ended. After it ends and the grace period passes, the organisation becomes read-only: everyone sees everything, changes and clocking are paused until renewal, and nothing is deleted.

payroll.title: Payroll (Owner and payroll staff)
payroll.body:
Payroll has its own permissions: the Owner holds them all and can give each one to a person, for their sites or the whole organisation. Set the components once under Payroll > Settings (earnings, allowances, deductions; a fixed component can apply to everyone with a default amount) and each employee's profile with effective dates. A cycle covers a period: open it, enter the month's variable amounts (or import a spreadsheet), review the attendance suggestions (unpaid leave, lateness, overtime) and the checks, then submit. Whoever submitted does not approve. Approval stores a frozen version; lock it to publish payslips. Reopening needs a reason and makes a new version. Reports: individual payslips, the detailed summary and the combined salary + allowances sheet, in PDF or Excel. Totals are kept per currency. Inside a cycle you can search and sort the people, copy each person's variable lines from their previous cycle as drafts, and add the same line to several chosen people at once (everyone or nobody). Payslips of an approved or locked cycle are exported in bulk on the server as one ZIP, each payslip with its own serial number; the file is downloaded through a short-lived link and deleted after 7 days. Insurance and taxes are calculated automatically in every new cycle under the country's law, with Egypt as the default: social insurance (employee and employer shares within the minimum and maximum insurable wage), salary income tax by brackets after the personal exemption and the employee's insurance, and the martyrs' fund. Every figure can be changed under "Insurance and taxes" in Payroll settings, with a button to go back to the country's values. On each person's profile: not insured, tax exempt, or a fixed insurable wage. Changes apply to new cycles only.

New: in Payroll > People press anyone (or search by name or code) to open one window with their whole salary: the code, the date new values apply from (the 1st of the month by default), the basic and every fixed item, insurance and tax - and one "Save everything" button. Unchanged values are not saved again, an emptied box ends the item, and any error shows inside the window with the item's name. Arabic digits are accepted in every amount. A deduction can be taken "before tax" (health insurance, union fee) and the monthly tax rounded down, from Insurance and tax settings.

payslips.title: My payslips
payslips.body: My payslips shows the payslips published to you from approved, locked cycles. Press "Request payslip" at the top, choose the month and add a note if you like: the person in charge of payroll gets a notification that opens straight on the manager page, on a card with a preview of the payslip and two buttons - "Send", which gives you a notification and the PDF by email and makes it appear here, or "Decline" with a reason that reaches you in a notification (you can ask again). What is sent is the approved copy as it is, never recalculated, and nobody but the person in charge sees it.

externalPay.title: External labour pay (inside External labour)
externalPay.body:
External labour pay is separate from employees and payroll, with its own permissions (seeing external workers on the dashboard shows no pay). Under Rates give each worker an amount, a currency and a unit - per day, week, month or year (or hour); a change applies from its date. Under Policy set the organisation's deductions and additions (a fixed amount in a currency, or a percentage of gross) and the day-rate rule for monthly and yearly rates (a fixed number of days, 30 by default, or the period's calendar or working days). A pay run covers a period: daily and hourly quantities come from the kiosk, weekly, monthly and yearly ones are entered, and a quantity unlike the kiosk needs a reason. Add individual deductions or additions with a reason - in days where the rate allows, otherwise as an amount. Approval freezes the run; changing it needs a reopen with a reason. Export one worker, a site or everyone in PDF or Excel; totals are per currency and drafts are marked. When an external worker is added, the rate can be entered at once: the amount, per hour, day, week, month or year, and the currency; it is changed later under "Rates" with a date it applies from.

New: "External labour" is one menu item with two tabs inside, "Workers" and "Pay". Someone who may only see pay opens straight on the Pay tab.

importedAttendance.title: Attendance from connected systems
importedAttendance.body: Another system - a fingerprint device or an HR system - can send clock-ins and clock-outs to PROSM Time through the API with a key the owner creates. Sending the same event twice does nothing. These events wait on the Manager Console under "Attendance received through the API" and count for nothing - not hours, payroll, the dashboard or leave - until the owner, or a manager who may correct that person's attendance, approves them. Approving turns each clock-in and the next clock-out of the same person into one attendance record, recorded in the action log; an event that overlaps attendance already recorded, or has no clock-out yet, stays with the reason. Rejecting needs a reason. Accounting and HR systems can also read employees, sites, attendance, leave and balances, shifts and the payroll of locked cycles through the same API.

integrationsApi.title: Integrations and the API
integrationsApi.body: The owner opens Settings, then Integrations and API, to create a key for an accounting, HR or other system and choose what it may read: employees (sensitive fields separately), sites, attendance, shifts, leave and balances, and the payroll of locked cycles; receiving attendance is a separate choice. A key is shown once, can be given an expiry date, and can be revoked at any time. Webhooks send a signed notice to the owner's HTTPS address when employees, attendance or leave decisions change; failed deliveries are retried and can be sent again. The technical description for developers is the API contract (openapi.json). Every request is recorded.

announcements.title: Notice board
announcements.body: Under Announcements everyone sees what was addressed to them - announcements and official statements, with links and files - and confirms reading when asked. Whoever may publish (managers for the sites they manage and their people; the owner or whoever manages announcements for the whole organisation, departments or anyone) writes the text, chooses the recipients - the whole organisation, sites, departments or chosen people - adds links (videos as links) and images, PDF or Office files up to 10 MB, and either publishes now or sets a time, with an optional expiry. "Publish only" notifies in the app and on the phone; "Publish with email" also emails each recipient. Files are kept privately and open only for the recipients, through a link that works for a few minutes. "Who read" shows who opened and who confirmed, within the publisher's own people. A published announcement is not edited; it can be withdrawn with a reason, and everything is in the action log.

departments.title: Departments
departments.body: The owner, or whoever manages departments, adds them in Settings. Each person belongs to one department at most: choose it when adding the person or on their page. Archiving a department keeps the people's history and stops it being chosen. Announcements can be addressed to departments.

employeeHome.title: The employee's home
employeeHome.body: An employee's home is one screen: the clock-in map and its buttons. The floating "My hours" button shows your hours for 15 seconds and closes on any tap; the "My clock-in reminders" button opens your own clock-in and clock-out reminders. On the phone, Home sits in the middle of the bottom bar; pressing it, or the PROSM logo, while on Home refreshes the page and takes you back to its top.

headerTools.title: Weather and quick search
headerTools.body: At the top: the temperature where you are now - press it for feels-like, humidity, wind, UV index, the day's high and low, and a refresh button. The search button (the magnifier, or Ctrl+K on a computer) opens any page of the app as you type its name.

updates.title: Updates
updates.body: On the web: when a new version is out a "New version available" bar appears; press it and the page reopens on the new version straight away. On Android: updates come from Google Play. Your data is kept on the server either way.

personPage.title: The person page (for administrators)
personPage.body: Press anyone in People to open their page in tidy cards: department, employment, leave, role, permissions, checks, devices (shown only when they have registered devices), and "Application Access", with blocking access and deleting their personal attendance data on request. A person's salary is managed in Payroll, not on their page.

myFile.title: My file
myFile.body: Menu → My file shows your details, contract, documents, warnings and incentives, attendance and leave. It is read-only: ask personnel to change your details. The Attendance tab of My file is the one place for your attendance: Summary (the last 30 days by site), Records (every clock-in in detail, the month and printing), Timesheets (ask for one and see yours) and Exceptions (the moments outside a work area that need your reason). The Attendance button at the bottom opens it. The Attendance and Timesheets pages in the menu are now the team's, for managers.

myDocuments.title: My documents
myDocuments.body: The documents your company needs from you appear in My file → Documents with their state (missing, expiring, expired). Tap "Upload" or "Renew": the camera opens, photograph the document and enter its dates. Without internet it is kept on the phone and sent later. Personnel review it; if refused you are told why. You are reminded before a document expires.

myPenalties.title: Warnings and incentives
myPenalties.body: When a penalty is decided you get a notification. Open it in My file → Penalties and incentives: "Received" means you have seen it, not that you agree. You can appeal within the time your company set, and if your reply is requested you write it there. Incentives appear there too.

penaltiesManager.title: Recording and approving penalties
penaltiesManager.body: Menu → Penalties and incentives. "Record a violation" for a person at your sites (with a photo from the phone); lateness and absence are recorded automatically by the bylaw. The bylaw chooses the penalty by how many times it happened. In "Waiting for me" you investigate, approve, reduce (with a reason) or refuse (with a reason). Whoever recorded a violation cannot approve it if the bylaw says so. You can also propose an incentive.

documentsAdmin.title: Employee documents
documentsAdmin.body: From a person's file → Documents press "Add a document": its name (or pick one already used), number, start date, end date when it has one, and a photo or PDF - it is recorded as valid at once. A document with an end date changes state by itself: valid, expiring, expired, and a reminder comes 30 and 7 days before the end date and on the day. Menu → Documents only shows: what has expired, expires soon, is missing or waits for review, with a CSV export; each line opens its person's file. When adding (or on any document) you can make it "Required from every employee": every file gets it as missing, and with an end date you can choose "No clock-in once it has expired".

bylaw.title: Penalties bylaw
bylaw.body: Settings → People → Penalties bylaw. First set your company's limits (deduction cap, days to appeal) and accept the notice - PROSM gives no legal values. Add violations with their ladder, set each penalty type's steps (investigation, the employee's reply) and approval levels, then publish from a date: it becomes a new version, posted in the Media Center for everyone to confirm reading. Recorded violations keep the version they were recorded under.

taxConfig.title: Tax and insurance
taxConfig.body: Payroll → Settings → Tax and insurance. Egypt is ready with PROSM's values, kept up to date. "Copy and edit" makes your own version (your company takes responsibility). For another country, enter the brackets, the exemption and the insurance categories. Try any salary in the calculator - it uses the payroll's own engine. Each save is a version from a month; cycles already made keep their rules. Only the owner changes the country, never with a cycle open.

q1.question: I forgot to clock out - what do I do?
q1.answer: Contact your manager - they can record the correct Clock Out on your behalf (the action is recorded as theirs, not yours), or approve a correction. If you are still clocked in after 12 hours the app asks once whether you are still working; after 24 hours the session is closed automatically and its hours wait for your manager's review before they count.

q2.question: Why was my Clock In flagged as outside my work area?
q2.answer: Your site has a configured geofence and GPS accuracy tolerance (or, with no site selected, your organization's own no-site radius around where you clocked in). If your reported location fell outside that area, you're asked to explain why so the right manager can review it - approving it clears the flag entirely; rejecting it caps your worked time at that moment.

q3.question: Which time is recorded when I clock in?
q3.answer: The server's time, always - changing your phone's clock has no effect. The only exception is an action made without a connection: it keeps the device's time, and if that differs from the server's by more than 2 minutes, it's marked for your manager to review.

q4.question: How do I change the language or theme?
q4.answer: Open the user menu (bottom of the sidebar) - Language and Appearance (Dark/Light/System) can be changed there at any time, and you can also set your profile picture from the same menu.

q5.question: I clocked in without choosing a site - why did it ask for a "workplace"?
q5.answer: Site is optional so you can register attendance from your real current location even when it isn't a registered site - but a short description of where you actually are is required in that case, so reports never show a blank site. Your organization's own no-site radius still protects that session the same way a real site's geofence would.

q6.question: What's the difference between Attendance Record and Timesheets?
q6.answer: Attendance Record is a live, date-ranged log of clock-in/out events - nothing to approve. Timesheets are a generated, period-based object (worked/break/overtime totals) that goes through a real submit -> approve workflow and gets locked once approved.

q7.question: Can I export my attendance or timesheet as a PDF?
q7.answer: Yes - Attendance Record, Timesheets and Allowances each have their own Export PDF action, scoped to whatever you're currently viewing, and Reports gathers the Attendance Record and Allowances exports in one dedicated place too. Each also has a Print button, and your home page links to all of them.

q8.question: Why can't I see some employees in People or Attendance Record?
q8.answer: You only ever see yourself, plus - if you manage a site - the people assigned to that site. The Owner sees everyone. This is enforced by the server, not just hidden in the interface.

q9.question: Does the desktop app sign me out every time I close it?
q9.answer: No - your session is remembered between launches, the same way it is on your phone or in a browser.

q10.question: Can I still play the radio while I'm clocked in?
q10.answer: Yes - it keeps playing in the background whatever your attendance status. It is called "Radio" in the sidebar (press it to open the stations list and search) and takes very little room when collapsed.

q11.question: How does the 30-day demo work?
q11.answer: On the welcome page, “Use the trial” opens the usual activation steps without a code, creating the organisation and its owner at once. The trial lasts 30 days (server time) and a bar shows the days left. A week before the end the owner gets a notification and an email with sales@prosm.net, info@prosm.net and support@prosm.net. When it ends the organisation becomes read-only, with nothing deleted: enter an activation code in Settings > Subscription, or ask PROSM to renew the licence, and everything works as before. One trial per email.

q12.question: Does attendance work without internet?
q12.answer: Yes. On your phone, Clock In, Clock Out, breaks and Change Site work with no connection, with the photo and location taken at that moment. They're kept encrypted on the device, in order, and sent automatically once when the connection returns - never twice. Times that differ from the server's are marked for review. Other pages need a connection.

q13.question: Why does my record say "Device time (offline)"?
q13.answer: That action was made without a connection and recorded with your phone's time, which differed from the server's by more than 2 minutes. Your manager sees it in Pending Review and can approve it or correct it.

q14.question: Who can see my location and photos, and for how long?
q14.answer: You, your site managers and your organisation’s owner. Location samples during a shift are deleted after 30 days and attendance photos after 90 days, or sooner if the owner shortened it. The live check keeps no face data — only the photo itself and the result. Your profile photo shows only inside your organisation. The privacy policy covers the rest.

q15.question: Does SOS call the ambulance or the police?
q15.answer: No. It alerts your site's managers, the Owner and co-workers on site, with your location. In an emergency, call your local emergency number yourself.

q16.question: Why can't I clock in?
q16.answer: Usually one of these: the phone is not giving a live location (turn location on and wait a moment), you are outside a site that refuses clock-ins from outside, you have approved leave today, or the organisation's subscription has ended and it is read-only. The message you see says exactly which.

q17.question: How do I ask for my payslip?
q17.answer: In My payslips press "Ask for your payslip". The payroll manager is notified; when they send it in the app it appears in My payslips, you are notified, and you can save it as PDF.

q18.question: Why does my manager see me as "outside" on the dashboard?
q18.answer: Because the last location your phone sent while clocked in was outside your site's zone, or you clocked in from outside and no new location has arrived since. Open the app at the site so your location updates; if you were outside for a reason, send it from "My exceptions".
